title: Converged Inference Protocols PRD and Go-to-market Checklist
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: This PRD defines a converged, developer-first API surface and operational checklist to launch the hosted inference endpoints that support chat, completions, embeddings and reranking with consistent semantics and predictable billing. Goal is a single, clear migration path for existing hosted users and a frictionless onboarding experience for new users.

Scope:
- In scope: API contract for /v1/inference (mode parameter to select chat/completion/embedding/rerank), OpenAPI and SDK changes, billing mapping for tokens vs embedding units, per-route quotas, streaming variants for chat and completions, structured output hooks, and rollout gates.
- Out of scope: Dedicated capacity UI changes (handled in a follow-up), deep model catalog UX, on-prem packaging changes.

User problems:
- Confusion between multiple overlapping endpoints that cause integration bugs and double-billing.
- Inconsistent streaming behavior across chat/completions.
- Lack of clear acceptance criteria and test harness for rerank outputs and embedding dimensionality.

High-level approach:
- Introduce a converged endpoint (/v1/inference) while maintaining compatibility shims for existing retro endpoints for 6 months.
- Provide explicit mode/version parameters and a mapping table that converts old API calls to the new contract server-side.
- Publish deterministic acceptance tests and a canonical test dataset to validate quality regressions for rerank and embeddings.
- Define metrics, dashboards, and rollback criteria before enabling GA.

Stakeholders:
- Product: Aisha Patel (owner), Marco Hernandez (PM lead)
- Eng: Runtime (lead: Priya Raman), API (lead: Daniel Cho), Billing (lead: Samir Gupta)
- Design: UX for API docs and Console (lead: Lina Torres)
- Solutions: Developer onboarding and migration docs (lead: Keisha Brown)

Non-functional requirements:
- Latency SLOs: median generation latency <= 120ms for short completions, tail latency p99 <= 2s for chat with streaming enabled (on hosted tier).
- Availability: 99.95% for hosted inference endpoints.
- Billing: Accurate mapping of tokens/embeddings to billing events; no double-counting across conversion shim.
- Security: All requests must support customer-supplied headers for tokenization and KMS reference for Private models.
acceptance_criteria: API contract published in OpenAPI spec and reviewed by API and SDK teams
Backward compatibility: 95% of existing API tests pass when run against the shim translation layer
Streaming parity: chat streaming and completion streaming behave identically for chunk boundaries and token-level metadata
Embeddings: dimensionality and norm are stable vs baseline for model versions (regression tolerance defined and validated)
Rerank: canonical rerank harness shows no >5% degradation on ranked-list recall across benchmark datasets
Billing: billing events emitted and end-to-end invoicing validated in staging with finance team
Console: per-route analytics show token counts, latency, error-rate and cost breakdown in retention window
Rollout safeguards: automatic fallback to legacy endpoint on error rate increase >150% or p99 latency regression beyond threshold
Documentation: migration guide, SDK examples, and code samples for Python/Node/Go published
Security review: completed and signed-off by security and compliance

decisions: Converged endpoint will be /v1/inference with 'mode' param: {chat,completion,embedding,rerank}
Streaming implemented using current SSE/HTTP2 semantics; no websocket variant in GA
Shim layer will remain for minimum 6 months; full deprecation timeline published at launch
Billing will emit discrete events tagged by 'unit_type' (token|embedding|rerank-call) to avoid ambiguity

qa_plan: Unit tests for each mode validating parameter parsing and payload shapes
Integration tests: legacy endpoint -> shim -> converged endpoint request translation
Performance tests: QPS ramp to validate CPU and memory overhead with and without shim
Chaos tests: simulate partial model unavailability and assert graceful fallback to alternate model versions
Regression tests: embedding vector stability and rerank ranking consistency using canonical datasets
rollout_plan: Canary 5% traffic in a single region for 48 hours with automated SLO checks
Expand to 25% additional traffic across two regions for 72 hours
Monitor and hold until billing events validate for selected customers
If health checks pass, enable GA and schedule public announcement and migration webinar
Begin planned deprecation communication for legacy endpoints with 6-month notice
metrics: Adoption: number of unique API keys using /v1/inference
Quality: rerank recall@10 and embedding cosine stability vs baseline
SLOs: median latency, p99 latency, error rate
Billing: discrepancy rate between expected and actual invoice line items
Reliability: availability percentage and incident count during rollout
